claims.claim_text: The indexed Edgar A. Prichard is the Oklahoma journalist and Army company clerk recruited into Donovan's organization.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index and NPS history align on the uncommon full name and direct OSS training connection.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the uncommon exact name and official OSS account align, although the NPS text omits the middle initial.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS explicitly places Army company-clerk service before recruitment and earlier journalism before that military role.
claims.match_notes: Box 620 remains unreviewed; no newspaper or Army unit is invented.

claims.claim_text: Prichard's immediate documented pre-OSS affiliation was service as a company clerk in the United States Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history expressly says Donovan's organization recruited him after his Army company-clerk service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact-name match and direct OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway; dates and unit remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The index supplies no rank, so commissioned or enlisted status is not inferred.

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, Prichard had worked as a journalist in Oklahoma.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS documents the occupation and state but does not name a newspaper, broadcaster, or other employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official biographical account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS occupation before Army service; employer and dates are unresolved.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS journalism employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Jerry M. Sage is the Procter and Gamble salesman and reserve officer recruited from Fort Lewis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index rank and uncommon name align with NPS's detailed West Coast sales, Army, COI recruitment, and Area B chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the exact first and last name, middle initial, commissioned career, and distinctive OSS instructor history align.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS dates civilian work to fall 1941, active duty to September 1941, and COI recruitment to March 1942.
claims.match_notes: The NPS article uses Jerry Sage without the middle initial; the rank and chronology provide additional corroboration.

claims.claim_text: Sage's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was active-duty Army service at Fort Lewis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS sequences his September 1941 active-duty request, training responsibilities at Fort Lewis, and March 1942 COI summons.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same detailed official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway from Fort Lewis to Donovan's organization.
claims.match_notes: The Army relationship is not counted as civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Sage's last documented civilian employer before active military duty was Procter and Gamble, where he was a West Coast salesman.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS places the named sales job in fall 1941 immediately before his September request for active Army duty.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same detailed official chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded last civilian employment before military service.
claims.match_notes: The organization is preserved under its historical spelling as found in the source.

claims.claim_text: The indexed USMCR Captain Elmer Harris is the Marine lieutenant and former General Petroleum Company salesman assigned to OSS Area B.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name, Marine service, officer rank, civilian occupation, and Area B assignment align across the NARA index and NPS history.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the source-index USMCR note is an especially specific corroborating identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS sequences civilian sales work, three months at Marine Corps School, and spring 1942 OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: The index rank reflects a later Captain grade while NPS calls him a Marine lieutenant during the 1942 transition.

claims.claim_text: Harris's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the United States Marine Corps, including three months at Marine Corps School.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS explicitly sequences Marine Corps School and his spring 1942 assignment to OSS Area B.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name, USMCR index note, officer rank, and Area B role.
claims.match_notes: Military service remains separate from the last civilian employer field.

claims.claim_text: Harris's last documented civilian employer before Marine Corps training was General Petroleum Company.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies him as a marine-use salesman for the company before the three-month Marine Corps School interval.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same exact-name and Marine-specific official account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded last civilian employment before military service.
claims.match_notes: The source does not supply exact employment dates; no modern successor name is substituted.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George H. White is the Federal Bureau of Narcotics investigator who became an OSS Area B undercover-work instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full indexed name and official NPS account align on the federal investigative career, Camp X training, and OSS instructional role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the middle initial, federal occupation, Camp X training, officer title, and OSS Area B role distinguish this common name.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places the bureau role and Camp X training before or at the beginning of Area B service in 1942.
claims.match_notes: Box 832 remains unreviewed; no unrelated postwar activity is needed for the employment claim.

claims.claim_text: White's probable immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Federal Bureau of Narcotics as an investigative agent.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS describes him as a leading bureau investigator who attended Camp X and then taught undercover work at OSS Area B.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact middle-initial name and unusually specific career sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate government pathway; the source does not provide a formal transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The uncertainty in administrative timing remains visible; the bureau is not mislabeled as a private employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Charles M. Parkin Jr. is the Penn State engineer and Fort Belvoir instructor recruited to teach OSS demolitions.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, engineering specialty, commissioned career, Fort Belvoir assignment, and OSS instructional role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the uncommon full name, senior rank, branch specialty, and detailed Area B chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS sequences Penn State, reserve training, regular Army commission, Fort Belvoir instruction, and OSS recruitment.
claims.match_notes: NPS omits the suffix in the narrative; NARA preserves Jr. Box 586 remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Parkin's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Army Corps of Engineers School at Fort Belvoir as an instructor.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he taught at Fort Belvoir for a year before Donovan's office summoned and recruited him for Area B.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same detailed official history.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian-employer claim.

claims.claim_text: Before his Army engineering career, Parkin was an honors engineering student and ROTC cadet at Penn State.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history documents the university, course of study, honors, ROTC participation, and progression to a regular Army commission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student affiliation before military service.
claims.match_notes: Penn State is not classified as Parkin's employer.

research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the immediate Army company-clerk pathway and earlier journalism occupation while leaving the newspaper or broadcaster unnamed.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 620, the NPS-cited address, and Oklahoma journalism directories.
